name: com.breadboardhub/circuits
title: breadboardhub circuits
description: Check, simulate and design electronic circuits, with a link to run each one live in the browser.

tools.name: check_circuit
tools.description: Checks whether a circuit is wired correctly: loose ends, parts with no power source, an LED with the wrong diode model, unknown parts, labels on top of parts. With "request", also checks that the parts asked for are there (a bulb, an ammeter, a voltmeter, a switch). Checks structure only, not voltages or currents. Takes a CircuitJS (falstad) circuit or a breadboardhub.com/sim link. Returns the problems found, the parts list and a link that opens the circuit running live in the browser. Free and instant, with no daily limit.

circuit.description: The circuit: CircuitJS (falstad.com/circuit) text, a "$" options line then one part per line such as "r 176 112 304 112 0 220" for a 220 ohm resistor (at most 20,000 characters), or a breadboardhub.com/sim link that carries one.

request.description: Optional: what the circuit is meant to be, in plain words, such as "a 9V battery, a switch and a bulb with an ammeter" (at most 1,000 characters).

tools.name: simulate_circuit
tools.description: Simulates a circuit and returns the voltage across and current through every part once it settles, such as the current through an LED, the output of a voltage divider or whether a bulb lights. Also names faults: a short circuit, nothing flowing, an LED over its current rating, a bulb too dim to light. Runs CircuitJS, a real circuit simulator, on a CircuitJS (falstad) circuit or a breadboardhub.com/sim link. Returns the readings, the faults and a link that opens the circuit running live. Takes 10 to 30 seconds. Daily limit per account; an API token raises it.

circuit.description: The circuit: CircuitJS (falstad.com/circuit) text, a "$" options line then one part per line such as "r 176 112 304 112 0 220" for a 220 ohm resistor (at most 20,000 characters), or a breadboardhub.com/sim link that carries one.

tools.name: sweep_circuit
tools.description: Runs a circuit across a range of values for one part, such as a supply from 5V to 12V or a resistor from 100 to 10k ohms, and returns the simulator's readings at each value. With "measure", also reports how one reading changes across the range: its lowest and highest value and the spread. Suits checking how a circuit holds up as a battery sags, or finding the part value that hits a target. Runs CircuitJS on a CircuitJS circuit or a breadboardhub.com/sim link. Up to 12 values without signing in, 25 signed in. Counts toward the daily simulation limit, one per 5 values.

circuit.description: The circuit: CircuitJS (falstad.com/circuit) text, a "$" options line then one part per line such as "r 176 112 304 112 0 220" for a 220 ohm resistor (at most 20,000 characters), or a breadboardhub.com/sim link that carries one.

sweep.description: The part to change and its values. A part is addressed by kind and index: index 0 is the first part of that kind in the circuit text. Kinds that can be swept: "voltage" (a DC voltage source, volts, under 24 V) and "resistor" (ohms, above 0).

part.description: A part by kind and zero-based index among the parts of that kind, in the order of the circuit text, such as { "kind": "resistor", "index": 1 } for the second resistor.

values.description: Either a range, { "from": 5, "to": 12, "steps": 8, "scale": "linear" } (steps counts the values, both ends included; scale "linear" or "log"), or a list, { "list": [5, 9, 12] }. Values may be numbers or strings with SI prefixes such as "4.7k".

measure.description: Optional: one reading to summarise across the sweep, such as { "part": { "kind": "led", "index": 0 }, "quantity": "current" }. Kinds as the readings name them: "voltage", "resistor", "led", "diode", "transistor", "capacitor", "ammeter", "voltmeter", "lamp" and so on.

part.description: A part by kind and zero-based index among the parts of that kind, in the order of the circuit text, such as { "kind": "resistor", "index": 1 } for the second resistor.

quantity.description: "current" through the part (amps) or "voltage" across it (volts). Default "current".

tools.name: design_circuit
tools.description: Designs an electronic circuit from a plain description, such as an LED with its resistor, a 555 timer blinker, a transistor switch, a voltage divider, or an Arduino or ESP32 breadboard project with its sketch. The design passes breadboardhub's structural checks, with one corrected attempt if needed; it is not simulated. Returns the circuit as CircuitJS text, any Arduino code, the check result, a link that opens it running live, and the parts list with DigiKey, Mouser and LCSC search links. Takes up to 2 minutes. Daily limit per account; an API token raises it.

description.description: What to design, in plain words, such as "a 9V battery lighting a red LED through a switch" or "an Arduino reading a potentiometer and dimming an LED" (10 to 1,000 characters).

tools.name: edit_circuit
tools.description: Changes an existing circuit as asked in plain words, such as "make the two resistors parallel", "add a voltmeter across the LED" or "use a 12V supply", or answers a question about it ("what does the 10 mH part do?"). Takes a CircuitJS circuit or a breadboardhub.com/sim link. The changed circuit passes breadboardhub's structural checks; a change that would break it is refused and the circuit comes back unchanged. Returns the new circuit, a link that opens it running live, and the parts list with supplier search links. Takes up to a minute. Counts toward the daily design limit.

circuit.description: The circuit: CircuitJS (falstad.com/circuit) text, a "$" options line then one part per line such as "r 176 112 304 112 0 220" for a 220 ohm resistor (at most 20,000 characters), or a breadboardhub.com/sim link that carries one.

change.description: What to change, or a question about the circuit, in plain words (3 to 1,000 characters).

purpose.description: Optional: what the circuit is for, in plain words (at most 1,000 characters). Helps keep the change in line with it.

tools.name: calculate
tools.description: Electronics calculators with exact answers: LED resistor, resistor color code, 555 timer, voltage divider, Ohm's law, series and parallel resistors, RC time constant, RC filter, transistor base resistor, capacitor code, PCB trace width, battery life, motor power supply, motor driver choice, robot battery runtime, servo power supply and servo power budget for many servos. Returns the answer, the working and a link to the circuit running live. Values may use SI prefixes ("4.7k", "100n"); inputs left out take example values, listed in the answer. Free and instant, with no daily limit.

inputs.description: The calculator's inputs by name, such as { "supplyV": "9", "ledV": "2", "currentA": "15m" } for led-resistor. Inputs by calculator: resistor-color-code (d1, d2, d3, exponent, tolerance); led-resistor (supplyV, ledV, currentA); voltage-divider (vin, r1, r2); rc-time-constant (ohms, farads, supplyV); ohms-law (volts, ohms); series-parallel-resistor (arrangement, r1, r2, r3, r4, supplyV); transistor-base-resistor (loadV, loadA, controlV, hfe, overdrive); 555-timer (r1, r2, farads, supplyV); pcb-trace-width (amps, riseC, oz, layer, lengthMm, supplyV); battery-life (capacityMah, activeMa, usablePct, volts, activePct, sleepMa); rc-filter (ohms, farads, hz); capacitor-code (code, tolerance); motor-power-supply (motorV, stallA, motors, driver, supply); motor-driver (motorV, runA, stallA); robot-battery-runtime (capacityMah, chemistry, cells, motorMa, drivePct, electronicsMa, usablePct, minV); servo-power-supply (servos, servoV, stallA, movingPct); servo-power-budget (g1Model, g1Count, g2Model, g2Count, supplyV, supplyA, stalled, movingPct, dutyPct, logicA, wireM, awg, wiring, connectorA, batteryMah, batteryC, customStallA, customAtV, customIdleA, customMinV, customMaxV). Band colors may be color names ("yellow"), d3 may be "none" on a 4-band resistor, and arrangement may be "series" or "parallel".

tools.name: debug_circuit
tools.description: Finds why a circuit someone built does not work, such as an LED that stays off or a 555 that does not blink on a breadboard. Takes the symptom and either the circuit or a description of what was built, which it draws as built. Simulates that and a proposed fix, and says if the simulator confirms the fix or the circuit as drawn works (so the fault is on the board). Returns the likely causes, its reading of a described circuit, live links to both circuits, checks to make on the board and the readings a working circuit gives. Takes up to 3 minutes. Counts toward the daily design limit.

symptom.description: What goes wrong, what was expected, and anything measured, such as "the LED does not light; the battery reads 9V" (3 to 1,000 characters).

description.description: What was built, drawn as built with any mistakes: the parts, their values and what connects to what, including which way round parts are, such as "9V battery + to a 470 ohm resistor, then the LED long leg, short leg to battery -" (up to 3,000 characters). Needed when no circuit is given.

circuit.description: The circuit: CircuitJS (falstad.com/circuit) text, a "$" options line then one part per line such as "r 176 112 304 112 0 220" for a 220 ohm resistor (at most 20,000 characters), or a breadboardhub.com/sim link that carries one.

tools.name: design_chip
tools.description: Designs digital logic in Verilog from a plain description, such as a 4-bit counter, a traffic light state machine or a logic circuit for an FPGA. Writes the module and a step-by-step test, builds it with Yosys and runs the test on the built circuit, correcting it up to twice. "verified" means it built clean and every test step passed; the AI wrote the test too, so it is returned for checking. Returns the code, the test and a link that opens the design with its diagram and waveforms. Takes up to 4 minutes. Counts toward the daily design limit.

description.description: The digital circuit wanted, in plain words, such as "a 4-bit counter with enable and synchronous reset" (3 to 1,000 characters).

tools.name: fix_chip
tools.description: Fixes Verilog that does not compile or gives warnings, such as syntax errors, width mismatches or unintended latches. Builds it with Yosys and Verilator, corrects it, and builds it again after each change. Returns the corrected code, anything still wrong, and a link that opens it with its diagram. Counts toward the daily design limit, except when the code already builds clean (then nothing is changed).

code.description: The Verilog source code, one or more modules (at most 20,000 characters).

tools.name: explain_chip
tools.description: Explains what a Verilog module does, in plain English: its inputs and outputs, its behaviour and anything unusual. Suits learning digital logic or reading FPGA code someone else wrote. Returns the explanation as text; nothing is built or changed. Counts toward the daily design limit.

code.description: The Verilog source code, one or more modules (at most 20,000 characters).

tools.name: search_designs
tools.description: Searches the public circuit, firmware and schematic designs people have shared on breadboardhub, such as "ESP32 temperature sensor", "buck converter" or "Arduino motor driver". Returns each design's name, type, tags, stars and link. Free, with no daily limit.

query.description: Words to search for, such as "esp32 temperature" or "buck converter" (2 to 100 characters).

limit.description: How many designs to return, 1 to 10 (default 5).

tools.name: get_design
tools.description: Gets one public design shared on breadboardhub by its owner's username and its slug, both shown in search results and in design links (breadboardhub.com/<username>/<slug>). Returns its name, type, description, licence, tags, simulator and link. Free, with no daily limit.

username.description: The design owner's username, as in breadboardhub.com/<username>/<slug>.

slug.description: The design's slug, as in breadboardhub.com/<username>/<slug>.

tools.name: list_practice_problems
tools.description: Lists breadboardhub's hardware interview practice problems: Verilog and RTL questions of the kind asked in FPGA, ASIC and digital design interviews, such as counters, FIFOs, state machines and arbiters, each graded by a hidden test. Filters by difficulty, topic, kind ("design" to write a module, "find-the-bug" to write a test that catches buggy versions) or the starter set. Returns each problem's id, title, difficulty, topics, suggested minutes and page link. Free, with no daily limit.

topic.description: Only problems with this topic, such as "fsm", "fifo" or "counter" (up to 40 characters).

kind.description: "design": write a module that passes the hidden test. "find-the-bug": write a test that passes the correct design and fails every buggy version.

starter.description: Only the starter problems, a good first set.

tools.name: get_practice_problem
tools.description: Gets one hardware interview practice problem by its id: the task, the module's name and ports, an example, three written hints from a nudge to the approach, and the starting point (an empty module, or for find-the-bug problems a starting test). The answer and the hidden test are not included. Returns the problem and its page link, where it can also be tried against a clock. Free, with no daily limit.

id.description: The problem's id, such as "gray-code-converter", as in breadboardhub.com/practice/<id>.

tools.name: submit_practice_answer
tools.description: Grades an answer to a hardware interview practice problem, exactly as the breadboardhub practice page does. For a design problem, send the Verilog module: it is built with Yosys, its ports are checked and the hidden test runs on it. Returns pass or fail, how many test steps pass, and the first failing step with its inputs and expected outputs, or the build errors. For a find-the-bug problem, send a test: it reports whether the test passes the correct design and how many buggy versions it catches. Signed-in accounts get the attempt saved to their progress. Counts toward an hourly build limit.

verilog.description: Design problems: the Verilog source, with the module name and ports the problem gives (at most 20,000 characters).

test.description: Find-the-bug problems: the test, as { "clock": "clk", "steps": [{ "set": { "rst": 1 }, "tick": 1, "expect": { "count": 0 } }] }. "set" drives inputs, "tick" applies clock edges, "expect" checks outputs; leave "clock" out for a design without one.

tools.name: list_embedded_problems
tools.description: Lists breadboardhub's C and embedded interview practice problems: firmware and robotics questions such as a timer rollover bug, register bit fields, a switch debouncer, a ring buffer, a quadrature encoder decoder, fixed-point filters, CAN frame packing and a PID step. Each is graded by hidden tests on an emulated ATmega328P. Returns each problem's id, title, difficulty, topics, suggested minutes and page link. Free, with no daily limit.

tools.name: get_embedded_problem
tools.description: Gets one C and embedded interview practice problem by its id: the task, the provided header (types and prototypes), the functions to write, an example, three written hints and the starting code. The answer and the hidden tests are not included. Free, with no daily limit.

id.description: The problem's id, such as "c-ring-buffer", as in breadboardhub.com/practice/embedded/<id>.

tools.name: submit_embedded_answer
tools.description: Grades a C answer to a C and embedded interview practice problem, exactly as the breadboardhub practice page does: the code is compiled with avr-gcc for the ATmega328P together with hidden tests and run on an emulated chip. Send only the functions the problem asks for (the header is provided). Returns pass or fail, how many test cases pass and the first failing call with its expected and actual value, or the compiler errors in the code. Signed-in accounts get the attempt saved to their progress. Counts toward an hourly build limit.

c.description: The C source: the functions the problem asks for (at most 10,000 characters).
